text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Blocks(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jumping(x) ::: x jumps when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Shooter(x) ::: x is a shooter.
Michael ::: Michael (constant).
Windy ::: Windy (constant).
Person(x) ::: x is a person.

Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → Blocks(x, y)) ::: If a man is taller than another man, the taller one can block the other's shooting.
Taller(Michael, y) ∀y (Person(y) ∧ y ≠ Michael) ::: Michael is taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If person x is taller than person y, and person y is taller than person z, then x is taller than z.
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
∀x (Shooter(x) ∧ Jumping(x)) → GreatShooter(x) ::: Every shooter who can jump when shooting is a great shooter.
¬Blocks(Windy, Michael) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.

Conclusion:
GreatShooter(Windy) ::: Windy is a great shooter.
